subject: INLA crashes using offset in formula

messages.author: c621ac38989fbf3c
messages.subject: INLA crashes using offset in formula
parts:
Hi,
 I'm trying to specify a Poisson model using a simple population offset:

form<-data$Count ~ data$ADI2 + f(idx, model="bym", graph=adj)

model <- inla(form, offset=data$Pop, data=data, family='poisson',
               control.predictor = list(compute = TRUE), control.compute = list(dic = TRUE))

Whenever I include this term INLA crashes. Am I coding this incorrectly?

Thanks,
Paul

messages.subject: Re: INLA crashes using offset in formula

On Tuesday, April 9, 2019 at 10:14:20 PM UTC+1, Paul Lantos wrote:
Hi,
 I'm trying to specify a Poisson model using a simple population offset:

form<-data$Count ~ data$ADI2 + f(idx, model="bym", graph=adj)

model <- inla(form, offset=data$Pop, data=data, family='poisson',
               control.predictor = list(compute = TRUE), control.compute = list(dic = TRUE))

Whenever I include this term INLA crashes. Am I coding this incorrectly?

Use offset(LogPop) where  logPop <- log(Pop)

And better avoid all that data$ stuff.

Alain
 

Thanks,
Paul

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Re: INLA crashes using offset in formula
parts:
Yes, the link function is 'log', so you're getting exp(Population ...)
if doing offset =Population

with the Poisson, there is an argument 'E' as well, doing

inla(..., family = "poisson", E = Pop)


see inla.doc("poisson")
